title: Authorise inside every state-changing route handler

facts.note: Routes are entries in the `routes` object of `Bun.serve` or branches of a `fetch` handler.
A file-content observer must detect any POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route entry or `req.method === "POST"`-style branch in scope, whether or not it was changed in this diff.
Emitted by bun_security_hygiene_detector for each mutating handler whose body has no recognised auth call.

fires: A `Bun.serve` routes object contains a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE entry (new or pre-existing) whose handler body contains no recognised authorisation call.
A `fetch` handler has a `req.method === "POST"` (or other mutating method) branch with no guard call inside that branch's body.
A mutating handler relies on an auth call made in a sibling route or elsewhere, not in its own body.
doesNotFire: GET or HEAD handlers (public reads, e.g. htmx fragment loads).
A mutating handler whose body calls a recognised guard (or a project guard whose name has been added to the recognised set).

given: A Bun route handler for POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE (a `routes` entry of `Bun.serve` or a method branch of a `fetch` handler) in non-test source.
when: The handler exists in the inspected source (any in-scope mutating handler, changed or not).
then: The handler body MUST itself call a recognisable authorisation guard before any write.
prefer: If the handler delegates to a wrapper that authorises internally, call it by a recognised guard name, or add the wrapper/project guard name to the rule's recognised set.
avoid: Relying on auth performed in a sibling route or another handler — it protects nothing for this handler.
Suppressing the rule because the project uses its own guard helper instead of adding that helper's name to the recognised set.
Adding auth requirements to GET/HEAD reads to satisfy the rule (out of scope; creates noise on the most common route in the codebase).
unless: GET and HEAD handlers are out of scope (reads).
why: A mutating handler with no auth call is the shape that leaks writes; public GETs are normal in a hypermedia/htmx app (how fragments load), so requiring auth on reads would be noise on the most common route — only mutating methods are checked, deliberately.
evidence: bun_security_hygiene_detector reports no SECURITY-MISSING-AUTH-001 finding for any mutating handler in the inspected non-test source.
Reviewer sees the guard call inside each mutating handler's own body, before any write.
verifier_detail: Detector finds each mutating route entry (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) or `req.method === "POST"`-style guard, brace-matches ITS handler body, and reports the handler when no recognisable authorisation call appears inside it.
mutating_route: a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE handler; GET (and HEAD) out of scope.

authorisation_step: a recognisable guard call inside the handler body. The recognised set is broad on purpose — the rule asks whether the author considered auth at this handler at all, not which helper they used; it does not enforce one blessed helper.
Project-specific guards or authorising wrappers are supported by adding their names to the recognised set.

Bun has neither decorators nor a DI container: routes are entries in the `routes` object of `Bun.serve` or branches of a `fetch` handler, and authorisation is an ordinary call (so detection is call-based, not signature-based).
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Original name: State-changing routes perform an authorisation check.
Aliases: SECURITY-MISSING-AUTH-001 — shared core alias, also carried by the agnostic node and its python-pytest realization.
Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED (not ported) for Bun: the python-pytest sibling matches a FastAPI decorator whose signature carries `Depends(get_current_user)`. Same obligation, new detector.
Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (implementation type validator, ref bun_security_hygiene_detector).
